rounds.text: Filtron Engineers Ltd trades at an astronomical P/E of 1892x according to filed statements, alongside an unsupportable EV/EBITDA of 109.39x that dwarfs the sector benchmark of 13.58x [E1, E11]. Operational returns are exceptionally poor, with filed statements confirming a ROCE of 0.7%, an ROE of 0.8%, and a median return on equity over the last year of just 1% [E12, E13, E20]. This anemic capital efficiency heavily lags behind sector benchmarks, demonstrated by an ROCE of 4.51% against a sector standard of 11.57% and an ROA of 3.3% versus 4.31% [E8, E10]. Valuation models severely penalize the stock, with a discounted cash flow estimating intrinsic value at Rs 1 per share against a market price of Rs 62.6, resulting in a staggering margin of safety of -4311.1% [E32, E33]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF implies that the current price requires an unrealistic 78.0% earnings growth rate, wildly detached from the 18.0% base case assumption [E34]. Conceded: the company boasts a P/B of 8.03x against a sector benchmark of 13.39x and an ROE of 6.89% against a sector benchmark of -8.3% [E7, E9].
